Apple | Software Engineer (ICT3) | San Diego | December 2021 | Offer
Hello Leetcode. Would like to tell you all about my experience interviewing at Apple for UMC team.

Four 1 hour interviews, with an hour break after the first two.

Interview 1 - Coding w/ Manager + Engineer
	*  First question was a Java question. Gave me a base class thats a library and another class that extends the base class. Asked me if there was anything odd about the class.
	* second question was similar to meeting rooms 2, but build out a method called `bookApi(int id, int startTime, int endTime)` that returns a boolean if we can book a room with id at the current timeslot
	* own rating - no hire, this round was terrible because the manager was lowkey yelling at me during the Java question and I kind of froze up.

Interview 2 - Coding with another manager and engineer
	* First question was [Median of two sorted arrays](https://leetcode.com/problems/median-of-two-sorted-arrays/)
	* gave the O(m + n) approach and could not get the optimal approach but was close
	* Second question was a Java related question. Gave me a class MovieIterator that needed hasNext() and next() implemented. pretty standard
	* own rating - soft hire but leading to no hire
break

Interview 3 - Coding with two engineers
	* First question was create checkerboard in HTML/JS (was rusty but got a working solution)
	* Extention of [First Last Pos of Element in Sorted Array](https://leetcode.com/problems/find-first-and-last-position-of-element-in-sorted-array/) but instead of the first and last index the output should be how many occurences of the element there are. 
	* own rating - soft hire

Interview 4 - Coding with two engineers
	* First question was a path finding question - given a list of obstacles and a 2d grid, start and end, return true if there exists a path
		* follow up was return the actual path 
		* did simple DFS, interviewer was satisfied with it
	* Second question was reverse linked list as a freebee, then [Reverse nodes in K Group](https://leetcode.com/problems/reverse-nodes-in-k-group/)
		* did the recursive method, interviewer did not ask me to optimize for space
	* own rating - first strong hire rating


Good experience overall in terms of seeing some improvement in my interviewing skills, just need to keep grinding and I'll get there eventually.

ineering concepts.

Overall Assessment Difficulty: Medium to Hard, primarily due to the tight time limit.

# Recruiter Call
About a week later, I received a call from an Apple recruiter.

What we discussed:

- My reason for looking out

- Why Apple?

- Compensation expectations

The recruiter was friendly and professional, and after our chat, I was moved to the next round: the technical interview.

# Technical Interview (Screening + Coding)
This was a 60-minute video interview with an Apple engineer.

- React Output-Based Question
The interviewer showed a small React code snippet involving the useContext API.

  - I was asked to predict the output and explain the reasoning.

  - I stumbled a bit but managed to convey my understanding.

  - Follow-up questions on React hooks:

    useContext: its use in prop drilling and state management

    useMemo & useCallback: optimizing performance in React components

Tip: Be crystal clear with hook behaviors under different re-renders and props changes.

- Nested Tabs Rendering Problem (Coding Round)
This was the main coding challenge — and also the most interesting one.

  - **Problem Statement**: Given a flat array of tab objects with id, name, and parentId, render a nested tab or accordion structure in React where each tab appears under its parent.

     Sample Input JSON:

    ```
    [
    { "id": 1, "name": "Parent 1", "parentId": null },
    { "id": 2, "name": "Child 1.1", "parentId": 1 },
    { "id": 3, "name": "Child 1.2", "parentId": 1 },
    { "id": 4, "name": "Parent 2", "parentId": null },
    { "id": 5, "name": "Child 2.1", "parentId": 4 }
    ]

    ```
    Objective:
    Transform this into a nested UI structure, like:

    ```
    - Parent 1
     - Child 1.1
     - Child 1.2
    - Parent 2
     - Child 2.1

    ```

  - My Approach: Converted the flat list into a tree-like structure using a map and used DFS to render tabs recursively.

  - I was able to solve it and explain my logic clearly. The interviewer seemed satisfied.

- Web Security Basics
  - Finally, I was asked a few questions on web security:

  - How can we secure a website?

  - Topics like HTTPS, Content Security Policy (CSP), CORS, and securing cookies came up.

# Outcome
After 4 weeks, I heard back from the recruiter:

**“Someone else has joined for this position. We'll reach out if similar roles open up.”**

He wanted distributed, P2P-first thinking: how nodes discover each other, how I would partition the crawl space without a coordinator, how I would handle nodes going offline mid-crawl. I adjusted and proposed a consistent-hashing approach for URL assignment with gossip-based failure detection. In the next part, he pushed on deduplication at scale and what would happen if the same URL gets assigned to two peers during a partition.

Second phone round was coding on CoderPad. The problem was similar to Basic Calculator II, a parsing and evaluation problem. The interviewer was focused on the code structure and how I was handling edge cases, and less on how fast I could complete it. He asked me to generate my own test inputs; I have seen this practice at other companies. We also talked through Java concurrency primitives and error handling strategies. That conversation felt more about production engineering than interview performance.

The onsite was virtual, six rounds, each 45 minutes. Horrible and shocking interview experience with Apple IS&T team
Hi LC community,
I wanted to share my horrifying interview experience with the Apple IS&T team, so that people can give a second thought before engaging with them. 

Starting with, I have a recruiter who has been extremely rude with me from Day 1. There were instances where this guy shouted on me for just asking him "how many total rounds of interview will be there". His words were - "You don't have to bother about upcoming rounds". I am not sure if he is this way or going through some personal crisis.

Moving on I had my DSA coding round scheduled. The interviewer looked sleepy and uninterested. There were no greetings and introductions and he went straight to the problem. He asked me an LC hard problem which is this - https://leetcode.com/problems/minimum-runes-to-add-to-cast-spell/ . My initial thought was I wont be able to solve it. But after some initial trying I could code it and run it through some test cases. It took me 40 mins to think and code the solution. I solve it with O(n+m) time complexity. As the interview was of 45 mins, in the last 5 mins the interviewer tells me he wants an optimised solution. I ask him what degree of optimisation he wants to which he remains silent.

Exactly 2hrs latter I get a generic rejection mail. I reach out to the recruiter for the interview feedback. I was shocked to the core to see how exaggerated and false the feedbacks were. The interviewer mentioned that I retracted back on my original solution and contradicted myself (which is absolutely false as I stuck with a single approach all through). He told that I didn't come up with an optimised solution despite hints (he was silent for most of the interview and the only hint he gave was you can travel in a matrix in all 4 directions :P). I told the recruiter this thing and he started getting defensive and started giving rude criticisms to me. He told me that they are Apple and their interview panel are some of the most experienced people in the industry. Asked him to talk in a professional tone and ended the call.
